sentenceSets.sentence: The policy aimed to extirpate the practice entirely rather than simply regulate it.

answerChoices.reasoning: Curtailing cuts something back while letting it continue at a reduced level, but the sentence sets the goal against regulation and marks it as total.
Discouraging works on people's willingness and leaves the practice available to anyone undeterred, which falls short of the completeness the sentence insists on.
Criminalizing attaches a penalty, which is itself a form of regulation and so belongs on the side of the contrast the policy rejects.
Supervision keeps the practice going under watch, the very alternative the sentence says the policy went beyond.
Studying the practice gathers information and changes nothing about whether it continues.
Taxing raises the cost of continuing the practice, which presumes it will continue.
Licensing formalizes permission to carry on, which is squarely on the regulatory side of the contrast.
Documenting records the practice and is not an aim a policy would set against regulating it.
Promoting the practice reverses a policy framed as going further than mere regulation against it.
Legalizing removes restrictions, the opposite direction from a policy that found regulation insufficient.
Funding the practice contradicts a policy aimed against it.

sentenceSets.sentence: Rats introduced by whaling ships extirpated the petrels from the island within forty years, leaving only bones in the dunes.

answerChoices.reasoning: Displacement moves a population elsewhere, but bones in the dunes and nothing else indicate the birds did not relocate.
Decimating implies heavy losses with survivors remaining, while the sentence leaves only bones behind.
Outcompeting describes an advantage in resources that plays out gradually, whereas the outcome recorded here is the petrels' complete disappearance from the island.
Harassment would disturb the birds without accounting for a colony reduced to skeletal remains.
Domestication would mean taming the petrels, which rats could not do and which bones in the dunes contradict.
Startling is momentary and cannot explain a change measured over forty years.
Colonizing describes what the rats did to the island rather than what happened to the birds.
Cataloguing is something naturalists do, not an effect rats have on a seabird colony.
Protection would have preserved the petrels, contradicting the remains left in the dunes.
Propagating would increase the birds' numbers, which conflicts with their disappearance.
Reintroduction brings a species back, the reverse of what the rats accomplished.

sentenceSets.sentence: She spent three seasons trying to extirpate the bindweed, digging out every last white root before it could run under the fence again.

answerChoices.reasoning: Pruning trims growth to shape a plant and keep it healthy, but she is going after the roots so that nothing survives to spread.
Containing would keep the weed within bounds, yet she is chasing the roots under the fence rather than settling for a boundary.
Transplanting moves a plant to a better spot, which is not the aim of someone digging out every last root of a weed.
Mulching suppresses growth by covering the soil, a surface measure that would not involve extracting roots one by one.
Feeding the bindweed would encourage the very growth she has spent three seasons fighting.
Harvesting gathers a crop for use, and nothing suggests she wants the bindweed for anything.
Photographing records the plant and leaves its roots exactly where they are.
Identifying the species is a first step, but she already knows what she is digging out.
Cultivating the bindweed would be the opposite of three seasons spent removing its roots.
Admiration is incompatible with digging the plant out root by root.
Propagating would multiply the bindweed she is trying to be rid of.
